evidence.title: INTERCEPTED TRANSCRIPT
evidence.body:
CHANNEL 7 // ENCRYPTED VOICE INTERCEPT // TRANSCRIBED BY SIGNALS UNIT
Four voices identified. Speaker labels are callsigns.

[00:14] CINDER: Channel's clean. Roll call, short answers. Lantern?
[00:19] LANTERN: Here. Key's on my belt. Same key I've carried since August, when they changed the lock.
[00:26] CINDER: Ferryman?
[00:31] FERRYMAN: Present. Key's in the van, van's behind the bakery. Don't ask which bakery.
[00:40] CINDER: Quill?
[00:44] QUILL: Listening. I don't carry a key. I only open doors from the inside.
[00:52] CINDER: Fine. That's three keys on this line, and one man who needs none.
[00:58] LANTERN: Saffron keeps asking to join the call.
[01:03] CINDER: Saffron carries the coffee, not a key. Leave her out of it.
[01:10] FERRYMAN: Old Marisol used to hold one. Should we worry?
[01:14] LANTERN: Marisol's key opens nothing now. They changed that lock in August. Forget her.
[01:22] CINDER: Now the plan. We move on the second Thursday of October, the night the vault is isolated for the audit. Not the first Thursday. Not the third.
[01:36] LANTERN: And Quill's post?
[01:40] CINDER: Quill stands at a panel that night. Whatever panel they give him on the night, that's our door.
[01:49] QUILL: Half the building mixes me up. Three of us sign our forms T.H. One guards Gallery C, one runs the canteen. I run vault systems, and I took the night-shift swap for the audit.
[02:04] FERRYMAN: What are we taking?
[02:08] CINDER: The red-wax batch. The second pour of the Anniversary bars, the one the Governor keeps bragging about. Not the blue seal. Not the first pour.
[02:19] LANTERN: I heard twelve thousand bars. Is that the count?
[02:23] CINDER: The count is noise. We need the lot number the Mint stamped on the red-wax pour.
[02:31] FERRYMAN: And proof we were inside?
[02:35] CINDER: One camera frame of Quill at his panel on the night. The Professor wants a witness on file. Nothing else matters.
[02:44] QUILL: The Professor left a note in the archive. Read it last.
[02:47] CINDER: Radio silence. Out.

evidence.title: NEWSPAPER FRAGMENT
evidence.body:
THE CAPITAL COURIER // THURSDAY 1 OCTOBER 2026 // PAGE 7

ANNIVERSARY SERIES TO REST IN SEALED VAULT

The Royal Mint will lock its Anniversary Series bullion away for the length of the annual audit, Governor Elena Vidal confirmed on Wednesday at a press briefing that ran forty minutes over its slot.

The series was cast in two pourings at the Refinery Annex over the summer. The first casting, closed with a cobalt-blue seal, was catalogued as Lot 29. The second casting, closed with a scarlet seal and described by the Governor as the one people will remember, was catalogued as Lot 47. Together the two castings come to roughly 12,000 bars and 1,800 kilograms.

A separate batch, the Heritage Run of 2019, also carried a scarlet seal (Lot 58). The Mint says that run was melted down in March and that none of it remains in the building.

The commemorative medals (Lot 63) will go on display in Gallery C from 15 October. Tickets are priced at 14 euros and the museum cafe, run by a local caterer, opens at 09:00. A sponsor has pledged 2.5 million euros towards the new conservation wing.

Rain is forecast for Thursday evening. Road closures are expected around Calle Mayor between 18:00 and 22:00, and visitors are advised to use the northern entrance.

evidence.title: PROFESSOR'S CIPHER NOTE
evidence.body:
To whoever reads this in the dark,

Three things open a vault: the door, the witness, and the metal.
The door is the panel where our man stood on the night the Mint went quiet.
The witness is the tag on the frame that saw him standing there.
The metal is the lot we came for.

The dial does not read numbers as they were found. It moves one step forward for every key carried on the line that night. Push every digit ahead by that many steps. If a digit runs past nine, let it fall back to zero.

Then enter them as a thief with manners would: the door first, the witness second, the metal last. Two digits each. Six digits in all.

Do not trust the loud numbers. They are only there to be ignored.

- P.
